name: Nonstick-coated cookware
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register; polymer-surface rows anchor it directly or by disclosed read-across, and metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows are controls because their dedicated release regimes are not yet ingested.
native_basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food), Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention
native_basis_label: specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT from the polymeric food-contact surface, µg/kg of food, determined by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V simulant, temperature and contact-time conventions. This is a MIGRATION basis and not a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell on this row is expressed per kg of material.
scope_note: Cookware whose food-contact surface is a cured fluoropolymer coating. Coatings are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, so the exact cell is unregulated and the published ceilings are a disclosed read-across from the plastics instrument, which is the nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis and is itself a fluoropolymer-compatible regime. The ceilings apply to the article as placed on market AND after the declared abrasion and thermal conditioning, because the certification question for a coated pan is whether the coating still isolates the substrate after realistic use; a pristine-coating result alone does not represent the article. Exposed interior rivets and any breached area are metal food-contact surfaces and fall to the alloy-release control regime under the component plan. This row is scoped to the ELEMENT panel; per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances are a separate and larger question that this standard does not address and does not imply anything about.
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Pb.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 2 lead non-detect requirement (0.01 mg/kg food)
Pb.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface is a cured liquid-applied coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Reg (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers in multi-material multi-layer articles but was not written for a sprayed and stoved coating system. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. The read-across is held to the coated article as placed on market and after the declared abrasion and thermal conditioning; the exposed-rivet and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the alloy-release control regime rather than by relaxing this value. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

tAs.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 2 total-arsenic non-detect requirement (0.01 mg/kg food)
tAs.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface is a cured liquid-applied coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Reg (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers in multi-material multi-layer articles but was not written for a sprayed and stoved coating system. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Arsenic is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list and the instrument states it as the total element, so this cell is total arsenic and cannot be satisfied by an inorganic-arsenic determination. iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no separate food-contact-material instrument anywhere in the credible set: every food-contact element requirement is written on total arsenic. Arsenic migrating from a polymeric food-contact article is in any case inorganic, so the total-arsenic non-detect requirement is simultaneously the tightest achievable inorganic-arsenic ceiling and bounds this cell by identity. No separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling is published, and inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic cell.
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration determination per the tAs cell; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total arsenic is detected at or above the detection limit.
iAs.bounded_by: tAs (read-across of eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd, total arsenic not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
iAs.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains. A cured polymer, a fired glaze, a metal alloy and a coated article contain no methylation pathway, and no credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for any food-contact material. The total-mercury non-detect requirement bounds any organomercury fraction that could be present. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published, and methylmercury never substitutes for the total-mercury cell.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury migration determination per the tHg cell; reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS on the migration extract only where total mercury is detected at or above the detection limit.
MeHg.bounded_by: tHg (read-across of eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd, total mercury not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food)
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.

Ni.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Ni.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 1 nickel SML (0.02 mg/kg food)
Ni.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface is a cured liquid-applied coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Reg (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers in multi-material multi-layer articles but was not written for a sprayed and stoved coating system. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Nickel carries a positive specific migration limit of 0.02 mg/kg food, the tightest positive SML in the Annex II element list. The read-across is held to the coated article as placed on market and after the declared abrasion and thermal conditioning; the exposed-rivet and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the alloy-release control regime rather than by relaxing this value. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface only; where a food-contact component of the article is a nickel-bearing alloy, that component sits in the alloy-release control regime described in this row's component plan, because the plastics SML was not written for and is not achievable by a bare stainless-steel surface.

Sn.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II lists no tin entry, and no credible sovereign sets a tin migration or release ceiling for a food-contact article of any material family. Tin is nonetheless a mandatory panel cell, because tin stabilisers in PVC compounds and tin-bearing solder are live pathways in parts of this category, so it is tested on every certified lot with no invented ceiling. This cell carries NO companion: the only sovereign tin numbers in existence are maximum levels on canned food, which are a FOOD basis on the contents of a tinplate container, and they are neither applicable to this row nor publishable as a migration ceiling. They are named as a companion only on the rows where a tinplate or crown component actually exists.
Sn.reference_method: EN 1186 / EN 13130 food-simulant migration testing on the finished article under its worst foreseeable use conditions (simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V; for repeat-use articles the third successive migration result governs), with ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant.

Cr.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cr.label: read-across of the EU 10/2011 Annex II point 2 total-chromium non-detect requirement (0.01 mg/kg food), relaxation declined
Cr.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface is a cured liquid-applied coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Reg (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers in multi-material multi-layer articles but was not written for a sprayed and stoved coating system. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. The read-across is held to the coated article as placed on market and after the declared abrasion and thermal conditioning; the exposed-rivet and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the alloy-release control regime rather than by relaxing this value.

Cr-VI.rationale: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 controls hexavalent chromium through the total-chromium requirement rather than through a separate species limit: total chromium must be not detectable, and the relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food value becomes available only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. HMTc declines that relaxation, so every certified article is held to total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, which bounds hexavalent chromium at or below the same value. No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium migration limit for a food-contact material, so no separate species ceiling is published; hexavalent chromium never substitutes for the total-chromium cell.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-chromium migration determination per the Cr cell; reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by ion-chromatography ICP-MS on the migration extract where total chromium is detected at or above the detection limit, and on any chromate-conversion-coated or passivated food-contact component regardless of the total result.
Cr-VI.bounded_by: Cr (read-across of eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd, total chromium not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, relaxation declined)
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2 sets the element requirement as a specific migration requirement on the food or food simulant, not as a limit on the material's element content. No credible sovereign sets a species-specific migration limit for this cell.
